Ecoregions are regions known to have similar floral species. Viridium’s ecoregions are based off of Armen Takhtajan’s 35 floristic regions:

1.  **Eurasian Circumboreal Region:** Contains most of Europe and Siberia north of the Mediterranean.
2. **American Circumboreal Region:** Contains the New-World side of the Circumboreal region including most of Canada, Alaska, and Greenland.
	- Includes island-exclusive Iceland subregion
3.  **Eastern Asiatic Region:** Contains temperate East Asia, bordered by the Gobi Desert and Himalayas.
	- Includes island-exclusive Japan subregion
4. **West Atlantic Region:** Includes Appalachia, the Piedmont, Coastal Plains, and Great Plains.
	- Includes Appalachia subregion
5. **Rocky Mountain Region:** Extends through the full range of the Rockies from southern Alaska to the San Francisco Bay.
6. **Mediterranean Region:** Includes all land north and south of the Mediterranean Sea, as well as Macaronesia.
	-  Macaronesian Region: Merged within the Mediterranean
7. **Saharo-Arabian Region:** Includes the Sahara Desert and Arabian Peninsula.
8. **Irano-Turanian Region:** Includes the mountains and steppes of central Asia and the northern extensions of the Near East and Anatolia.
9. **Madrean Region:** Includes the arid coast of California and most of northern Mexico including the Sierra Nevada.
10. **Guineo-Congolian Region:** Contains central and equatorial Africa’s tropical regions excluding Madagascar.
11. **Sub-Saharan Region:** Includes subarid east Africa, including the Ethiopian Highlands
	- Includes Socotra endemic subregion
	- Includes Danakil Depression subregion
	- Usambara-Zululand Region: Included in the Sub-Saharan Region.
12. **Karoo-Namib Region:** Includes arid and semi-arid areas of southwestern Africa including the Namib Desert and Cape provinces.
	- Includes the Cape Province endemic subregion.
	- Cape Region: Merged into the Karoo-Namib region as an endemic subregion.
13. **Madagascan Region:** Includes Madagascar.
14. **Indian Region:** Includes all of the Indian subcontinent and Sri Lanka up to the Himalayas.
15. **Indochinese Region:** Includes all of mainland southeast Asia.
16. **Indonesian Region:** An island-exclusive region including all of Indonesia, New Guinea, and the Philippines
17. **Polynesian Region:** Island-exclusive region including all southern Pacific islands save for Hawaii.
	- Fijian Region: Merged into Polynesian Region
	- Neocaledonian Region: Merged into Polynesian Region
18. **Hawaiian Region:** Island-exclusive region including the Hawaiian and Midway archipelagos.
19. **Caribbean Region:** Region including the Upper and Lower Caribbean archipelagos and the Bahamas, as well as most of southern Mexico and Central America. May exist as a continental or island region.
	- Includes Caribbean Islands subregion and Galapagos Islands endemic subregion
20. **Amazon Region:** Includes the Amazon Rainforest and all other tropical regions of northern South America, including the Llanos grasslands and Guiana highlands.
	- Guiana Highlands Region: Merged into the Amazon province as a mountainous subregion.
21. **Brasilian Region:** Includes all of non-Amazonian southern Brazil, extending to the north of Patagonia.
22. **Andean Region:** Includes the Andes Mountains of northern Chile, Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia.
23. **Outer Australia Region:** Contains the northeast and southwest corners of Australia.
	- Includes Tasmania island subregion.
	- Southwest Australia Region: Merged into the Humid Australia Region.
24. **Outback Region:** Includes the Australian Outback.
25. **Patagonian Region:** Contains the southern Andes, Patagonia, the Faroe Islands, and the northern tip of Antarctica.
26. **Zealand Region:** Contains New Zealand and all subantarctic islands.
27. **Antarctic Region:** Contains the Antarctic continent biome and sub-Antarctic biomes and islands surrounding it, including New Zealand’s Sub-Antarctic Islands.
    - Subantarctic Region: Merged into the Antarctic region.

- Fernandezian Region: Removed
  
## Temperature Regimes

Polar -> Subpolar -> Boreal -> Temperate -> Subtropical -> Tropical

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Zone 0 – Superpolar (Antarctica)
- Zone 1 – Polar
- Zone 2 – Subpolar
- Zones 3-4 – Boreal
- Zones 5-9 – Temperate
- Zones 10-11 – Subtropical
- Zones 12-13 – Tropical

## Humidity Regimes

Super-Arid -> Arid -> Dry -> Average -> Moist -> Humid -> Superhumid

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Dark Red – Arid
- Red – Sub-Arid
- Orange – Dry
- Yellow – Average
- Mustard – Wet
- Light Green – Humid
- Dark Green, Blue – Superhumid

## Altitudinal Belts

Submontane -> Montane -> Subalpine -> Alpine -> Snow

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- 0-100m – Submontane / Foothill zone
- 80-180m – Montane Zone
- 140-250m – Subalpine Zone
- 200-500m – Stratus Cloud Zone
- 210 – 320m – Alpine Zone
- 270m + – Snow Zone
- 320m + – Dead Zone
- 400m-1200m – Nimbus/Cumulonimbus Cloud Zone
- 600-2000m – Cirrus Cloud Zone
- 5000m-12000m – Nacreous Zone (Polar Only)

The overlap between zones is meant to simulate the gradient of plants over time. Trees can grow rarely in the subalpine zone, but no higher.

## Environmental Settings

Open – Forest – Hill – Mountainous – Desert – Wetland – Lacustrine (Lake) – Riparian (River) – Coastal – Marine

All plants can be placed on grasses and dirts, but those with specific substrate requirements can also be placed there and will only spawn on their preferred substrate. Trees that have a preferred substrate will only have their saplings grow if they are planted on this substrate, unless a fertilizer like bone meal is used.
